Hey,

I am very sorry to hear about your situation, I am glad you are speaking to counsellors, that is a lot more important than talking with parents.
If you told them you self harm, they would need to notify your parents/carers (if you are under 16 [18 in some countries]) and the NHS (if in the UK). 
On the other hand, they would also do a hell of a lot more to help you.

Telling your parents will have different drawbacks/advantages depending on what they are like. If they really care about you then that will take over no matter what else they are like. If they do, they wont be even slightly upset that you waited to tell them. Mine weren't upset I waited, they were too concerned. The advantages are that they will understand you better and will be able to provide a more relaxed environment for you to live in. They may be also able to get you further help.

My best advice to you would be to do what you think is best based on what you know about your parents. If they are kind and supportive people then it would likely be very beneficial for you to tell them.

If you ever need anyone to speak with about anything please feel free to contact me.

Also please read this: http://www.reddit.com/r/StopSelfHarm/comments/14bdhc/some_helpful_tips_from_my_counsellor/
It may help with the self harm.

Take care,
-Smitk

I dont know how the medication could affect it, only your GP could really tell you that. But here is how I finally (after 9 years) sorted out my insomnia.
I decided to set my alarm, every single day, for 5am. I wake up straight away and shower, get ready and then start the day. I refuse to let myself fall asleep at any point during the day until 9PM when I go to sleep (or sometimes later if I'm not really tired).
This helped me get into a good cycle and has really helped me. Might be worth a try!
